newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai cabinet approves 99 bln baht spending cuts.
newsitem.headline: Thai cabinet approves 99 bln baht spending cuts.

text.p: Thailand's cabinet approved on Tuesday 99 billion baht in spending cuts for fiscal 1996/97 (October-September), deputy finance minister Chavarat Chanveerakul said.
He told reporters after a cabinet meeting that 59 billion baht would be in the form of budgetary cuts while 40 billion baht would be cuts in spending by state enterprises.
No further details were immediately available.
Financial markets and investors had been waiting anxiously for a final cabinet decision on the cuts which had been recently proposed by Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan.

The cuts are aimed at curbing unnecessary government spending at a time when the national economy was facing a slowdown and serious attempts were being made to curb a wide current account deficit which amounted to 8.2 per cent of gross domestic product in 1996.
